describes: packages/plugin/stage: page turns in paged flow off pans, the drag bracket and the fling, and the pages you are on.

cases.name: a-wheel-turns-past-an-edge-it-began-at
cases.covers: In paged flow a stream of pans turns the page only at an edge it began at: reading down to the bottom stops there. After a 200 ms pause a push of 60 px past the bottom turns to the next page at its top, a shorter one turns nothing, and the rest of the stream that turned moves nothing. A push past the top turns back to the previous page at its bottom. listCurrentPages names the page you're on.

cases.name: a-drag-turns-on-its-release
cases.covers: A drag is one stream however long it holds: its pushes past the edge turn nothing until the release, which turns once the push and the finger's overshoot reach 60 px, and the release fling then moves nothing. An elastic drag pulled far past the edge turns instead of springing home; one pulled less springs home and stays.

cases.name: a-flick-turns-and-a-pinch-never-does
cases.covers: A release short of the push turns on a flick of 600 px/s past the edge; a slower one turns nothing. A pinch in the drag never turns the page, nor does the fling after it.

cases.name: a-sideways-push-turns-and-rtl-mirrors-it
cases.covers: A page that fits the view sits at every edge, so a sideways push turns it: leftward for the next page left to right, rightward right to left, and the other way back to the previous page. At the last page a push turns nothing. turnGestures: false and continuous flow leave turning to nextPage and previousPage.

cases.name: list-current-pages-names-the-spread-that-fits-across
cases.covers: listCurrentPages gives the pages you're on: the current spread while it fits across the view however tall (before placement too), else the current page; nextPage and previousPage step past those pages.

cases.name: a-wheel-at-the-end-of-the-pages-is-left-to-the-page
cases.covers: wheelBy (13305a14b) pans like panBy and answers whether the view took the wheel. A stream (the wheels up to a 200 ms pause) is decided by its first wheel: one that begins at the end of the pages with nowhere to go is left to the page around the viewer (false), every later wheel of it too, a zero wheel included; one that begins with room is the view's and stops at the end, holding what follows. Between streams a zero wheel is kept. scrollChaining: false keeps every wheel.

cases.name: a-new-push-ends-the-stream-that-coasts
cases.covers: A trackpad's next push begins before the last one stops coasting (138c54fe7): a wheel whose speed (distance over the wheels' own time) reaches 2.5 times the slowest the scroll had slowed to is a new push and begins a new stream with no pause. Stopped at the end, the view holds the coasting wheels and leaves the new push to the page; wheels more than 40 ms apart tell no speed, so mouse notches never read as a push.

cases.name: a-new-push-turns-on-from-the-page-a-coasting-turn-reached
cases.covers: In paged flow a wheel past the bottom with a page to turn to has somewhere to go, so the view takes it and turns the page; the coasting wheels after the turn move nothing, and a new push told from their speed (138c54fe7) begins a new turn stream that scrolls the page that arrived.
